title: Break it down
brief: Agents fail on big, fuzzy tasks and succeed on small, verifiable ones. Turn an epic into ONLY a JSON array of 4 to 8 tasks. Each task: {"id": "T1", "title": ..., "depends_on": [task ids], "done_when": a verifiable check}. Tasks are numbered T1, T2, ... and the first task has no dependencies.

lesson.summary: Decomposition turns one risky leap into a sequence of small, checkable steps. Each task should be small enough for one agent session, state what it depends on, and say how you'll verify it's done.
lesson.why_it_matters: This is how agent orchestration works in practice: a planner breaks work into tasks, workers execute them in dependency order, and each 'done_when' becomes an automated gate. Vague tasks produce vague results.
lesson.strong_example:
Break the epic into 4–8 tasks. Return ONLY a JSON array of {"id": "T1", "title", "depends_on": [], "done_when"}. done_when must be objectively verifiable.

hints: If you gave each task in the output to a different agent, would each one know when it's finished?
This is task decomposition. Ask for a fixed number of small tasks, explicit dependencies, and a verifiable completion check per task, and fix the exact JSON shape, including how ids are numbered.
Try: 'Return ONLY a JSON array of 4–8 objects {"id": "T1", "title", "depends_on": [ids], "done_when"}. T1 has depends_on []. done_when must be a test or observable check.'
reference_prompt:
You are a tech lead breaking an epic into tasks that coding agents will execute one at a time.

Epic: {{epic}}

Return ONLY a JSON array (no markdown, no explanation) of 4 to 8 task objects with exactly these keys:
- "id": "T1", "T2", ... in order
- "title": a short imperative description
- "depends_on": an array of earlier task ids (T1 must have [])
- "done_when": one objectively verifiable condition, such as a passing test or an observable result

Each task must be small enough to complete in one focused session.
